stash.gain_key_why: every dungeon loot table (data/cobblers/loot_table/dungeons/...) gets a table-level minecraft:set_custom_data {cobblers_dg_gain:1b}, so an item taken from a vault, bank or cache chest, or given by `loot give` (the fossil bay), is recognisable in the inventory for the one tick before the sweep moves it to the stash. The key is stripped when the item enters the stash, so a delivered item stacks with ordinary ones
stash.loot_table_prefix_why: only the dungeons' own tables. NEVER data/cobblemon/loot_table/fishing/pokerod.json (tools/dungeon_extras2.py overrides that GLOBAL path; its in-pocket branch is a separate cobblers table, which is under this prefix)
stash.absorb_radius_why: an item entity within this many blocks of a live member (dg.st 3..4, in cobblers:pocket) is moved into the stash the tick it is seen: a block's drop (pickup delay 10 ticks), a wild Pokemon's on-entity drop, a fished item (spawned at the bobber, pulled towards the player) all pass inside it before they can be picked up
stash.skip_item_entity_fields_why: an item entity with a Thrower was dropped by a player (their own item: never risked); one with an Owner is a `give` overflow or a delivery (the rift pick, a relic, a refund, our own exit delivery). ItemEntity's saved keys in 1.21.1 are Age, Health, Item, Owner, PickupDelay, Thrower (the 1.21.1 jar, class cjh)
stash.skip_item_tags_on_ground_why: a Poke Ball on the ground in a run is the player's own ball handed back (a throw at a Pokemon that cannot be caught drops it), never a find: kept. The tag is Cobblemon 1.8.2's own (data/cobblemon/tags/item/poke_balls.json in the jar). A ball from a chest is still risked: it reaches the inventory with the gain key
stash.skip_custom_data_keys_why: relics are kept (the owner, 2026-10-23); the pick, the satchel and the lent rod are the engine's; a sigil is a refund. Checked on item entities as well as the Owner field, so a relic dropped on a full inventory is never stashed
stash.fungible_why: items that stack to 64 in vanilla and whose plain form has no components: the stash keeps them as a count per id (any amount) instead of one entry a pickup, and gives them back in stacks of 64. Anything else, or any of these carrying a component, is kept as the exact stack it was

satchel.item_why: its use is a vanilla statistic: FoodOnAStickItem.use (the 1.21.1 jar, class ctz) awards Stats.ITEM_USED server-side on every right-click while not riding, so `minecraft.used:minecraft.carrot_on_a_stick` counts a use (the stat's criterion form, as EXP-073 step 2 proved for minecraft.mined)
satchel.name: Run Satchel
lore: What you find in a rift goes in here.
Leave by the exit to keep it. Die and it is gone.

view.entity_why: a vanilla merchant's trade screen is the one clickable item screen a datapack can show: its offers carry real item stacks (the stash's own NBT), every one out of stock (uses = maxUses) so the screen shows each item and its tooltip and nothing can be taken. A wandering trader needs no profession and never despawns with DespawnDelay 0; NoAI, Invulnerable, Silent, PersistenceRequired, DeathLootTable minecraft:empty. The Offers.Recipes record shape is the one tools/gulch_mine.py:1281 summons
view.name: Run Satchel
view.open_line: Right-click the satchel in front of you to look inside.

exit.choice_why: the choice is offered after a clean exit, in the overworld; unanswered for 60 s (counted only while online) it is Take it all, so an exit never loses an item
exit.bonus_why: DESIGN numbers for trainer-balance-designer: selling the satchel at the exit pays the bank's own price (CobbleDollars' bank list, tools/markets.py bank_prices: the base pack's then ours) plus a small bonus by band and for a run whose boss fell. Small on purpose: the bank buys the same items at the same price in any town
exit.price_source: tools/markets.py bank_prices (base-pack/cobbleverse/config/cobbledollars/bank.json, overridden by modpack/config/cobbledollars/bank.json, which tools/bank.py writes from data/bank.json)

lines.worth: The bank pays $%d for what it buys from it (with this run's bonus).
lines.unsold: It does not buy the rest; that comes to you either way.
lines.taken: Your Run Satchel is emptied into your hands.
lines.pay_failed: The bank could not pay. Everything comes to you instead.
lines.auto: No answer, so the Run Satchel is emptied into your hands.

death.lost_line: Lost with the run: your Run Satchel and everything in it.

modes.dry_run: every catch in a run is logged with its Pokemon UUID; a run that ends by any way but a clean exit looks each one up in the party and the PC and LOGS what it would remove. Nothing is removed. The default until the owner turns removal on
modes.remove: the same, and a logged Pokemon still found is removed by its UUID (remove_by_id) only if the player is out of battle, it holds no item, and (in the party) it is not the party's last Pokemon. Anything else is kept and logged

catches.uuid_source: q.pokemon.id in the pokemon_captured callback: Pokemon.getUuid().toString() (Cobblemon 1.8.2 jar, PokemonMoLangFunctions lambda$0)
catches.remove_source: q.player.party.remove_by_id(uuid) / q.player.pc.remove_by_id(uuid): iterates the store for Pokemon.getUuid() equal to the parsed UUID, returns 0 when none, else PokemonStore.remove's result (Cobblemon 1.8.2 jar, PokemonStoreMoLangFunctions lambda$6)
catches.exempt_why: the owner: 'everything you get should be risked, except cool catches'. A shiny (q.pokemon.is_shiny, Pokemon.getShiny) and any species a dungeon's prize can be at any band (tools/dungeon_prize.pool_at, rare and legendary, and the roster's spine boss) are never logged, so no removal can name them (an absence, the strongest anchor: docs/research/notes/dungeon-catches-on-the-clock.md section 6)
